headline: New Break closes $523,820 flow-through financing for its Timmins-area gold project
dek: The CSE-listed junior issued 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 each to fund drilling at its Moray gold project near Timmins, Ontario.
caption: A drill rig in a boreal forest clearing, representative of the exploration funded by the financing.

sources.title: New Break Closes $523,820 Non-Brokered Flow-Through Financing

unverified_claims: The characterization of continued drilling at the Moray project rests on the company's own description in its release; no technical or assay results were disclosed.
brief: New Break Resources Ltd. has closed a non-brokered private placement of 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 each for gross proceeds of $523,820, the company said. The CSE-listed junior will use the funds for Canadian exploration expenses at its Moray gold project, about 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario.

New Break paid $12,012 in finder's fees and issued 54,600 finder warrants, each exercisable at $0.22 for 24 months. Control person Patricia Quigley purchased 455,000 of the flow-through shares, which the company described as a related-party transaction relying on exemptions under securities rules. The shares carry a hold period expiring March 4, 2027.

The company said the gross proceeds will be renounced to purchasers as flow-through mining expenditures with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The financing remains subject to final approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange.
body: New Break Resources Ltd. has closed a non-brokered private placement of 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of $523,820, the company said. The shares qualify as "flow-through shares" under the Income Tax Act, and the proceeds will be used for Canadian exploration expenses, which qualify as flow-through mining expenditures under the same legislation.

The proceeds will fund continued drilling at the company's Moray gold project, located approximately 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, New Break said. The company will renounce the Canadian exploration expenses to the purchasers of the flow-through shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026. The financing closed November 3, 2026, and remains subject to final approval from the Canadian Securities Exchange.

New Break paid $12,012 in finder's fees in connection with the closing and issued 54,600 finder warrants, each exercisable into one common share at a price of $0.22 for a period of 24 months, the company said. The flow-through shares themselves carry no warrants and are subject to a hold period expiring March 4, 2027.

Patricia Quigley, described in the release as a "control person" of the company, purchased 455,000 of the flow-through shares in the offering. New Break said the issuance constitutes a related-party transaction under applicable securities rules, but qualifies for an exemption from the formal valuation and minority-approval requirements because it does not exceed 25 per cent of the company's market capitalization.
